To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a minimum concentration of metal precursor and a minimum potential difference are required to achieve a core-shell structure in bimetallic catalysts prepared by a one-pot reduction method in microemulsions.

the metal segregation of bimetallic nanoparticles is determined by three main factors: (1) the difference in the reduction standard potentials; (2) the flexibility of the microemulsion; and (3) the metal precursors’ concentration.

the metal segregation is the result of a combination of the metal reduction rate, the material intermicelle exchange rate and the metal concentration, and that the minimum difference between reduction rates of the metals is 0.20V.

the development of new methods for the synthesis of metal nanoparticles with controlled composition and structure, which are of great interest in the field of nanotechnology and nanocatalysis.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the metal segregation in bimetallic nanoparticles prepared from microemulsion by a one-pot procedure can be controlled by the microemulsion composition, metal concentration, and metal precursors reduction rate.

a bimetal catalyst with a core-shell structure can be prepared in a one-pot microemulsion method if the following three conditions are fulfilled: (i) The reduction rate of the metal precursors is different enough to allow the reduction of one of them to occur first; (ii) The microemulsion composition is such that the metal precursors can diffuse between the micelles; and (iii) A minimum concentration is reached to avoid the formation of alloy.

a core-shell structure can be obtained only by a combination of the following conditions: (i) a minimum difference between the standard potentials of the metal precursors of 0.2 V, (ii) a minimum metal precursors concentration (depending on the difference between standard potentials and the microemulsion composition) and (iii) a minimum microemulsion flexibility.

the metal segregation of bimetallic nanoparticles prepared by a one-pot microemulsion method depends on the difference in the reduction potentials of the metal precursors, on the microemulsions flexibility around the micelle, and on the metal precursors concentrations.
, by using a microemulsion as reaction media, it is possible to control the architecture of bimetallic nanoparticles.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the metal segregation in bimetallic nano-catalysts prepared from a microemulsion is the result of a complex interplay among the metal reduction kinetics, the material intermicelle exchange rate, and the metal precursor concentration.
the preparation method of bimetallic nanoparticles is crucial for the control of the metal segregation.

the preparation of bimetallic nanoparticles with a core-shell structure is possible in a microemulsion by means of a one-pot procedure if a difference of at least 0.2 V between the reduction standard potential of the metals is present.
